NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Visiting storytellers describe Isola all wrong: invite them to see village life, or correct the story at their own festival.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Storytellers from another island have been performing a tale about Isola in which the villagers are mysterious, silent people who live in trees and speak to fish. (friend) heard it at their festival and came home furious. (subject) thinks the storytellers simply do not know any better. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village invites the storytellers for a week. They see the gardens, the arguments, the terrible singing, the babies, the jokes. They go home and change the story. Now the Isolans in it are loud, funny and very bad at sitting still. (friend) says that is closer.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) paddles to the next festival and tells the real story, right after theirs. The audience is confused by two completely different Isolas. Some believe one, some the other. The storytellers are not pleased.
